items.q: A business has an opening cash balance of £10,000 for March. Cash inflows in March are £50,000 and cash outflows are £65,000. What is the closing balance?
items.why: Net cash flow = inflows – outflows = £50,000 – £65,000 = –£15,000. Closing balance = opening balance + net cash flow = £10,000 – £15,000 = –£5,000.
items.label: New question

items.q: An investment costs £160,000. Net cash flows are Year 1: £100,000; Year 2: £80,000; Year 3: £50,000; Year 4: £80,000; Year 5: £90,000. What is the payback period?
items.why: After 1 year the cumulative cash flow is £100,000, so £60,000 is still needed. In year 2 the business receives £80,000, about £6,667 a month. £60,000 ÷ £80,000 × 12 = 9.0, so about 9 months. Payback = 1 year 9 months.
items.label: New question

items.q: An investment in new equipment has these expected net returns. Year 0: net return (£50,000), discount factor 1.00. Year 1: £13,000, 0.95. Year 2: £28,000, 0.91. Year 3: £27,000, 0.86. Calculate the payback period.
items.why: Cumulative net return: end of Year 1 = £13,000; end of Year 2 = £41,000. £9,000 is still needed in Year 3, when £27,000 comes in. £9,000 ÷ £27,000 × 12 = 4 months. Payback = 2 years 4 months.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2017 Q16

items.q: Investment: Year 0 = -£1000k, Year 1 = £500k, Year 2 = £900k. ARR after 2 years = ?
items.why: Total returns = 500 + 900 = £1400k. Total profit = 1400 - 1000 = £400k. Average annual profit = 400/2 = £200k. ARR = (200/1000) x 100 = 20%. ARR = (average annual profit / initial investment) x 100.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A business employed an average of 270 people during the year and 35 left. What is its labour turnover?
items.why: Labour turnover = number leaving ÷ average number employed × 100 = 35 ÷ 270 × 100 = 13%.
items.label: New question

items.q: The network shows the activities in a project (durations in days). What is the length of the critical path?
items.why: Node 2: earliest start = 5. Node 3: the largest of A+B = 8, A+C = 10 and E = 12, so 12. Node 4: 12 + 3 = 15. The critical path is E–D, taking 15 days.
items.label: New question

items.label: Paper 1 June 2017 Q17

items.q: A single-product firm has weekly total costs of £80,000 and profit of £20,000. Labour costs are 42% of turnover and labour costs per unit are 84 pence. Labour productivity is 25 units per employee. Calculate the weekly output in units.
items.why: Turnover = total costs + profit = £100,000. Labour costs = 42% × £100,000 = £42,000. Output = £42,000 ÷ £0.84 = 50,000 units. (The productivity figure is not needed: it would tell you there are 2,000 employees.)
items.label: Paper 1 June 2018 Q16

items.q: A product has an income elasticity of demand of +2. Average real incomes rise by 3%. What happens to demand?
items.why: % change in demand = YED × % change in income = +2 × +3% = +6%. A positive YED means a normal good: demand moves the same way as income.
items.label: New question

items.q: The chart shows a business's inventory over time. How many units does the business use each day?
items.why: Inventory falls from 450 to 50 units, a fall of 400 units, over 4 days. 400 ÷ 4 = 100 units a day.
items.label: New question
